newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian utility Electrabel net profit up five pct.
newsitem.headline: Belgian utility Electrabel net profit up five pct.

text.p: Belgian utility Electrabel said on Thursday a combination of productivity gains and higher gas and electricity sales due to the cold winter outweighed lower prices to lift net profits five percent.

It reported group net profits for the six months to the end of June rose to 20.16 billion francs ($648.6 million) from 19.25 billion in the first half of 1995. It also predicted a good performance in the second half of the year.
Consolidated net profits rose to 18.11 billion francs from 16.63 billion.

"Barring any new circumstances, Electrabel's estimated profit for the current year means the company can plan to distribute a dividend that is at least equal to that distributed for the last financial year," the company said in a statement.

The firm said electricity sales to households rose 4.5 percent, although these was a 2.8 percent fall in sales to industry due to the economic slowdown. It noted a slight pickup in economic activity towards the end of the period.
Due to tariff reductions introduced in April the average price of electricity provided to households fell 2.1 percent, while prices for the industry remained stable.
Electrabel said the full effect of the tariff cuts would not be felt until the second half of the year.
Gas sales, on the other hand, surged 18.3 percent due to the hard winter.
The effects of this sales boom were, however, dampened by an average 3.8 percent cut in sales prices due to the lower prices of imported natural gas. ($ = 31.08 Belgian Francs)
